messages:
liam: heads up - production longctx service started hitting OOMs and p99 spikes right after we rolled PR #4923 (batching heuristics + kernel-router tweaks). noticed higher kv cache fragmentation in the heap profiles. anyone else seeing this?

maya: saw alerts ~10:12 UTC, matching canary. repro in staging with long sequences (32k-ish) - memory climbs and never releases. suspect eviction scan change.

owen: perf-ci flagged a regression on the runtime perf test: longctx_throughput_v2 dropped 18%, p99 up 4x. link: https://ci.internal/perf/4821

perf-ci: [alert] regression detected: job longctx_throughput_v2 failed thresholds (p99 latency +400%).

samir: quick logs: kernel-router picked fallback_kernel_opt instead of asm_fast for ~40% of steps at seq>16k after the change. that kernel uses an intermediate tensor that doubles peak mem per request.

liam: can you paste the stack/profile lines?

maya: here's a short heap diff from the profiler (staging):
```
# before (baseline)
kv_cache_frag_bytes: 120MB
active_buffers: 48MB
peak_native: 620MB

# after PR #4923
kv_cache_frag_bytes: 580MB
active_buffers: 210MB
peak_native: 1.8GB
```

maya: also saw eviction-scan timeouts in the logs: "evict_scan: scanned 1.2M entries, paused due to latency_slo"

owen: that eviction-scan pausing rings a bell - PR changed the scan stride and introduced a small sleep in the background compactor to avoid CPU spikes. might be starving compaction when many long sequences are active.

samir: bisecting locally: reverting the stride change in allocator branch makes fragmentation go back down and kernel-router picks asm_fast again. suspect interplay: allocator change altered alignment which made the kernel selection heuristic believe buffers were too fragmented for asm path, so it chose the slower path with higher transient memory.

liam: nice bisect. can we get a minimal repro and a quick revert in canary?

deploy-bot: canary rollout for runtime/2026.03.15-4923 -> started on infra-canary-3

maya: repro steps: run lm_eval with sequence lengths [8k, 16k, 32k] with synthetic prefix cache hits. command:
```bash
./tools/run_perf --model redwood-open-13b --seq-lens 8000,16000,32000 --concurrency 8 --prefill-cache
```

owen: I pushed a revert PR that undoes allocator stride tweak: https://git.internal/r/redwood/+/r/4947. requesting hotfix cherry-pick to canary.

liam: deploy the revert to canary, monitor p99 and memory. roll forward if good.

deploy-bot: revert PR r/4947 merged. starting canary rollout.

perf-ci: retest triggered for longctx_throughput_v2.

maya: early canary numbers look promising: p99 back to baseline, peak_native down ~650MB. still need to run longer to validate regression under sustained load.

samir: opened a ticket INS-2387 to track: root cause analysis + follow-ups: (1) unit test for kernel-router to prefer asm path when alignment ok, (2) eviction/compaction watchdog so compactor can't stall, (3) perf test permutations for seq-lengths to catch this mixing.

liam: add opt-level telemetry for kernel selection and allocator alignment so we can detect this class of interactions earlier.

owen: agreed. I'll add a small integration test that runs the eviction scanner under high longctx churn.

liam: thanks all. next: leave revert in canary for 12h, then decide on full rollout. :thumbsup:

maya: FYI: forwarded logs to infra-sre for cluster-level memory correlation.

samir: note for postmortem - the regression only showed up for mixed sequence workloads where prefix cache kept a lot of in-flight KV segments. single-long-request workloads didn't spike the same way.

liam: good catch. closing the immediate alert. follow-up in INS-2387.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for revert r/4947 -> success on infra-canary-3 (3/3).

perf-ci: longctx_throughput_v2: baseline restored. regression cleared.

owen: leaving this thread with the key repro and the ticket. will update INS-2387 with full bisect notes and bisection commit range.

liam: outstanding work: postmortem, tests + telemetry. thanks everyone.
